dedupe_keys.name: technical and economic aspects of load following with nuclear power plants oecd nea june 2011

description: This case study is an OECD Nuclear Energy Agency report of June 2011 on the technical and economic aspects of load following with nuclear power plants. Nuclear plants are mostly run as base load, the most economical and technically simple mode, where power changes are limited to frequency regulation and safety shutdowns, but countries with high nuclear shares or with ambitions for renewable energy ask whether plants can follow load regularly, including daily demand variations. The report, initiated within the NEA study System effects of nuclear power, considers this capability and the issues raised in a load following mode, giving a detailed analysis of technical and economic aspects and summarising the impact on the operational mode, fuel performance and ageing of large equipment components. Comments came from Electricité de France, Areva GmbH, E.ON Kernkraft and reactor manufacturers. Coverage is mainly countries with load following experience; the pages read do not itemise them. Access: 53-page PDF, free. Caveats: dated 2011. It suits operations control and flexibility studies of nuclear generation, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
